rfi.title: Southern African farmers prepare for powerful El Nino with agroecology
rfi.description: Farmer Dudzai Matsapa works under a scorching sun, digging small, shallow pits across his field in Nyanga, east of the Zimbabwean capital, Harare. He will later fill these potholes with organic manure and wait for the rainy season. This is all part of Matsapa’s preparation for the anticipated El Nino, which is expected to trigger drought and extreme heat across southern Africa.

rfi.description: How do you spot an artist? Are they the one with the jaunty beret or the dapper silk scarf? Or the tunic covered in paint? An exhibition at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris looks at how wardrobe choices have shaped society’s perception of artists – and made some of them into icons.

rfi.title: Love story: literary speed dating in an age of declining readership
rfi.description: This week saw France hand out its biggest literary awards, the Prix Goncourt and the Prix Renaudot. However, reading is on the decline, with only 56 percent of French people describing themselves as regular readers in 2025, down 5 percentage points from 2023. But might those numbers rise if reading was a way to meet your soulmate?

rfi.title: Nigeria's plan for state police raises hopes for security and fears of abuse
rfi.description: Nigeria this week took a step closer to a major overhaul of its security system after 28 of its 36 states approved a constitutional reform that would allow individual states to establish their own police forces. rfi.title: Suez Crisis at 70 reveals the humiliation France tried to keep hidden
rfi.description: Seventy years after France, the United Kingdom and Israel invaded Egypt following its nationalisation of the Suez Canal, the military operation is remembered as a diplomatic disaster. Friday marks the anniversary of a ceasefire that halted the fighting under international pressure, despite the invading forces' success on the battlefield. Archive footage excluded from French cinema newsreels shows the humiliation that followed, as Europe's colonial powers faced the limits of their influence.

Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult's base near the beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the Shakahola forest massacre.

rfi.title: Tanzania opposition leader Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for incitement

observador.description: Descartes postulou que os animais são destituídos de mente racional. Mas, ao contrário do que é corrente ler-se e ouvir-se, a maioria dos nomes cimeiros do pensamento iluminista rejeitou esta visão.

observador.title: IA ajuda a combater falta de vacinação em Moçambique
observador.description: Um quarto das crianças moçambicanas nunca recebeu qualquer vacina. Uma plataforma de IA, agora em expansão para 80 distritos, está a mudar esse cenário.

observador.title: Bruna paralisa voos e cruzeiros na Madeira
observador.description: Quedas de árvores, inundações e cinco desalojados. O aeroporto permanece condicionado e avisos amarelos mantêm-se. Agitação marítima prevista até segunda-feira.

observador.title: Messi revalida título de goleador da MLS pela 2ª vez
observador.description: Com 26 golos em 31 jogos, o argentino de 39 anos é o primeiro a revalidar o título de melhor marcador do campeonato norte-americano de futebol. Inter Miami estreia play-offs frente ao Columbus Crew.

observador.title: Fogo de Espanha domado no Sabugal
observador.description: Chamas que entraram em Fóios, no Sabugal, já foram controladas. Do lado português, 122 operacionais e dois meios aéreos mantêm vigilância no terreno.

observador.title: PS e Chega reclamam 23 milhões para agricultores açorianos
observador.description: Ministro da Agricultura diz que autorização europeia para os apoios extraordinários caducou em 2024. Oposição acusa governos da AD de enganarem os agricultores.

observador.title: Um morto e 28 resgatados ao largo de Creta
observador.description: O bote com migrantes sudaneses foi localizado pela Frontex a seis milhas da costa sul de Creta. É o segundo acidente na zona em três dias, com 59 desaparecidos do naufrágio anterior.

observador.title: Stradivarius e estreias absolutas em "Música em S. Roque"
observador.description: Pela primeira vez, a Temporada da SCML encerra em Mafra. O violoncelo Stradivarius "Chevillard-Rei de Portugal", tesouro nacional, será tocado na abertura e no fecho.

observador.title: Morreu Richard Lloyd, guitarrista dos Television
observador.description: O guitarrista, figura central do punk nova-iorquino dos anos 1970 e do lendário CBGB, morreu em casa, em Chattanooga. O cancro foi diagnosticado em março.

observador.title: Proteção Civil sinalizou 145 ocorrências até às 10h de hoje
observador.description: Funchal foi o município mais afetado. Cinco pessoas foram desalojadas em Santa Cruz. Avisos amarelos em vigor, com vento forte e agitação marítima até segunda-feira.

observador.title: 21 mortos em naufrágio de migrantes no Senegal
observador.description: O naufrágio ocorreu numa rota usada por migrantes para chegar às Canárias. Ministro espanhol do Interior esteve em Dacar a pedir reforço da cooperação.

spiegel.title: Evolution der Haustierhaltung: »Die Jungaffen versuchten, auf Schweinen zu reiten«
spiegel.description: Nicht nur Menschen schaffen sich Hunde und Katzen an. Der Anthropologe Cyril Grüter berichtet, dass auch andere Primaten Beziehungen eingehen, die an Haustierhaltung erinnern. Warum tun sie das?

spiegel.title: »Dass es eine heftige Rolle ist, wusste ich – aber ich hatte keine Ahnung, wie heftig«
spiegel.description: In der ARD-Serie »Friesenjunkies« gibt Sylvie Meis ihr Hauptrollendebüt. Nun erzählt die bekannte Moderatorin, warum eine Masturbationsszene sie Überwindung kostete – und trotzdem »spannend« war.

spiegel.title: Angst vorm Altwerden: »Wollen Sie den End-of-Life-Service wirklich nutzen, Herr Gutsch?«
spiegel.description: Ich fürchte mich vor dem hohen Alter. Vor Einsamkeit und Verfall. Meine Hoffnung? Ein freundlicher KI-Pflegeroboter – mit Sterbehilfekompetenz.

spiegel.title: Dave »Dinger« Bell: Extremsportler rudert allein im Boot über zwei Ozeane
spiegel.description: Der Brite Dave »Dinger« Bell ist allein 28.700 Kilometer durch zwei Ozeane gerudert. Dem SPIEGEL schildert er, welche Herausforderungen er dabei meistern musste – und wie er die Einsamkeit auf dem Wasser überstanden hat.

spiegel.title: Israel: Gadi Eisenkot erhält Auftrag zur Regierungsbildung – eine fast unlösbare Aufgabe
spiegel.description: Der Netanyahu-Rivale Eisenkot erhält den Auftrag, eine neue Regierung in Israel zu bilden. Die Aufgabe ist fast unlösbar. Drei Optionen gibt es.

spiegel.title: »Tatort« heute aus Zürich: »Frei wie ein Adler« im Schnellcheck
spiegel.description: Born to be weich: In dieser Zürcher Rocker-Soap geht ein Biker mit einem Jungen aus einer Downsyndrom-WG auf Verbrecherjagd. Ein »Tatort« wie ein Zuckerschock.

spiegel.title: Vanessa Emde: Weigerung zum Mandatsverzicht zeigt Hilflosigkeit der Linken-Spitze
spiegel.description: Die Linkenspitze um Elif Eralp wollte die umstrittene Abgeordnete Vanessa Emde zum Mandatsverzicht drängen. Deren Weigerung legt die Hilflosigkeit der Führung offen: Sie kann radikalste Kräfte in der Partei nicht bändigen.

spiegel.title: Sachsen: 74-Jähriger kippt 50 Kilo Fische auf Feldweg – einige Tiere überleben
spiegel.description: In Sachsen wollte ein 74-Jähriger offenbar eine große Menge Fische loswerden – und kippte sie an einem Feldweg aus. Gegen den Mann wird nun ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Sondervermögen: Bislang kaum Geld in Bildung, Betreuung und Wissenschaft geflossen
spiegel.description: Für die Bereiche Bildung, Betreuung und Wissenschaft waren für 2026 über eine Milliarde Euro aus dem Infrastruktur-Sondervermögen vorgesehen. Bislang wurde aber nur ein Bruchteil des Geldes abgerufen.

spiegel.title: Markus Wolf: Russlands Geheimdienst würdigt Ex-DDR-Spionagechef
spiegel.description: In der Bundesrepublik war DDR-Spitzenfunktionär Markus Wolf lange nur der »Mann ohne Gesicht«, bis er 1979 enttarnt wurde. Vor 20 Jahren ist er gestorben – in Russland erinnert man sich gern an ihn.

spiegel.title: Tübingen: Unbekannte kippen 15 Kilo Zement in Georgsbrunnen
spiegel.description: Eine Passantin in Tübingen hat in der Nacht beobachtet, wie drei Männer mehrere Zementsäcke in den Georgsbrunnen kippten. Die Behörden stellten erst einmal das Wasser ab.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Mann hisst Palästina-Flagge vor dem Reichstag
spiegel.description: Die Flagge der Einheit am Boden: Vor dem Reichstag in Berlin hat am Sonntag kurzzeitig eine Palästinaflagge geweht. Die Polizei hat zwei junge Männer festgenommen.

spiegel.title: Willie Nelson findet, er habe lange Zeit »alles falsch gemacht«
spiegel.description: Neben der Musik ist Country-Urgestein Willie Nelson vor allem für den Konsum von Cannabis bekannt. Mit 93 Jahren legt er nun Memoiren vor – und verrät seine Idee eines glücklichen Lebens.

spiegel.title: Dave Bell: Brite rudert 28.000 Kilometer von Südamerika nach Afrika
spiegel.description: Haie, Stürme und ein Whisky vom König: 327 Tage war Dave Bell allein in einem Ruderboot und durchquerte zwei Ozeane. Einsichten eines Mannes, der zwar lange allein war – aber nie einsam.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München: Manuel Neuer fällt nach Sehnenteilriss aus
spiegel.description: Seit diesem Wochenende ist Manuel Neuer der älteste Bundesligaspieler in der Geschichte des FC Bayern. Die kommenden Wochen dürfte allerdings Jonas Urbig im Tor der Münchner stehen: Neuer fällt vorerst verletzt aus.

spiegel.title: Beziehung: Wie Sie nach Enttäuschungen wieder lieben lernen
spiegel.description: Eine große Enttäuschung, Liebeskummer über Jahre, blind für Neuanfänge: Hier erklärt eine Psychologin, ob Liebe süchtig machen kann. Und wie Sie es schaffen, den Kopf wieder freizubekommen.

spiegel.title: Thomas Markle Jr. – Philippinen: Polizei entschuldigt sich bei Halbbruder von Herzogin Meghan
spiegel.description: Thomas Markle Sr. sitzt in den USA in Haft. Er soll Aufnahmen von Kindesmissbrauch gespeichert haben. Die Behörden nahmen auch seinen Sohn ins Visier, offenbar wegen eines Missverständnisses.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München: Uli Hoeneß glaubt an Rückkehr von Vincent Kompany bis Ende November
spiegel.description: Bayern-Coach Vincent Kompany erholt sich derzeit von einer Hirnhautreizung, hatte deshalb gar ins Krankenhaus gemusst. Ehrenpräsident Uli Hoeneß ließ nun durchblicken, wann Kompanys Comeback bevorsteht.

elpais.title: Alberto Núñez Feijóo: “Hacer una coalición de Gobierno con Vox no depende de mí”
elpais.description: El candidato del PP, en una entrevista en EL PAÍS: “Sánchez está consiguiendo desactivar a toda la izquierda y absorberla” |“Abascal nunca me ha hablado de vicepresidencias ni ministerios” | Confirma que derogará los decretos de vivienda y avisa de que, si el próximo fiscal general hace una propuesta penal contra Sánchez, no se lo impedirá

elpais.title: Sánchez reenfoca la campaña del PSOE en la gestión y asegura que blindará las pensiones en la Constitución
elpais.description: El presidente considera “un insulto a la inteligencia” que Feijóo sostenga que no depende de él que gobierne con Abascal

elpais.title: Los deberes económicos tras el 29-N: vivienda, infraestructuras, Presupuestos y  pensiones, entre los más urgentes
elpais.description: El partido o la coalición que logre formar un Gobierno tras las elecciones se encontrará un país que crece, con menos paro y deuda, pero que ofrece también grietas estructurales que hay que afrontar cuanto antes

elpais.title: “Nena, dime algo”: el último mensaje del marido de una víctima de Urda
elpais.description: Javier Barrio relata en una carta la desesperación que vivió con sus hijos mientras esperaba noticias de su esposa

elpais.title: Iñaki Barrón: “El ferrocarril tiene mucho que envidiar en seguridad al modo aéreo, sobre todo en entrenamiento”
elpais.description: El expresidente de la autoridad de investigación ferroviaria CIAF y portavoz del Comité de Seguimiento del Accidente de Urda del Colegio de Ingenieros de Caminos, reclama más formación a los profesionales del tren y una auditoría urgente del sistema ferroviario

elpais.title: “Parece un Kennedy”: Jon Ossoff, la estrella en ascenso del Partido Demócrata para 2028
elpais.description: El senador, respaldado por Obama y a quien se ha comparado con el expresidente, es el favorito en las casas de apuestas como candidato a la presidencia en las próximas elecciones

elpais.title: Trump cae derrotado en las urnas, pero aún es poderoso (e impredecible) en política exterior
elpais.description: El presidente de EE UU ha comenzado a dar pistas sobre sus próximos pasos con el nombramiento del radical Stephen Miller como nuevo jefe de Gabinete

elpais.title: Entre la muerte MAGA y la radicalización del trumpismo: los republicanos buscan su sitio tras la debacle electoral
elpais.description: La elección del radical Stephen Miller como jefe de Gabinete indica que Trump no tolera una reflexión interna sobre el futuro del partido tras la derrota en las ‘midterms’

elpais.title: Los demócratas que huyen de lo ‘woke’
elpais.description: Una nueva (y exitosa) generación de candidatos pertenecientes a minorías han decidido dejar atrás los debates identitarios para centrarse en los problemas de los electores. Y ha funcionado

elpais.title: Esta victoria no basta: ¿qué deben hacer ahora los demócratas?
elpais.description: El Partido Demócrata pasa por un momento de euforia que no se vivía desde la elección de Barack Obama en 2008. Pero el reto que hay por delante, derrotar a Donald Trump en las presidenciales de 2028, exige, según el historiador Michael Kazin, abandonar elitismos y transmitir empatía hacia los hombres y mujeres corrientes, además de mantener la coalición entre el ala izquierda y el ala moderada del partido

elpais.title: De viaje con Kiko Veneno: “Soy pesimista con el mundo, pero mi actitud vital es seguir poniendo rumba”
elpais.description: Acompañamos al autor de ‘Volando voy’, ‘Lobo López’ y ‘Joselito’ durante un viaje de semanas de encuentros, charlas, reflexiones y momentos vividos. Tras medio siglo de carrera, sigue igual de curioso y rebelde que en los setenta y saca nuevo disco fiel al “espíritu de los músicos ambulantes”, dispuesto a dar candela para comprender la realidad

elpais.title: ‘La revuelta’ cancela la presencia de su público previsto para la entrevista con Santiago Abascal, según personas invitadas al programa
elpais.description: Varios usuarios en redes sociales han asegurado haber recibido un correo electrónico en el que cancelaban su asistencia “por circunstancias especiales” que no se han aclarado

elpais.title: La guerra por la herencia de Brigitte Bardot enfrenta a un marido desheredado y una fundación animalista
elpais.description: Casi un año después de la muerte del icono del cine francés, la pareja con la que compartió sus últimos 30 años de vida ha entrado en una batalla con la organización creada por la actriz y a la que dejó todo su patrimonio. El próximo 9 de noviembre se cerrará su testamento ante notario, y su hijo ha aceptado sin rechistar las últimas voluntades de su madre

elpais.title: Mucho debate y pocas risas: El humor político no logra el salto televisivo nacional desde ‘Polònia’ o ‘Vaya semanita’
elpais.description: En una época en la que las tertulias están en todas las cadenas, la apuesta por la comedia es pequeña, salvo por formatos veteranos de los canales autonómicos que fracasaron en su salto a España

elpais.title: El reto de la maternidad en personas con discapacidad intelectual: “Yo tenía claro que quería ser madre, aunque fuera de uno”
elpais.description: La esterilización forzosa de estas mujeres quedó prohibida en España en 2020. Judit Seculi Horta y Salvador Ribas Payà crían a su hijo Aleix, de 5 años, con el acompañamiento de profesionales

elpais.title: Las mujeres pierden terreno en la empresa y la política tras décadas de progreso
elpais.description: La presencia femenina en puestos de liderazgo ha retrocedido en el mundo en paralelo a la ola reaccionaria de los últimos años. El deterioro de las políticas de igualdad ha dado alas a los viejos patrones sexistas

elpais.title: El mundo tras la derrota de Trump
elpais.description: El fiasco republicano disminuye la autoridad del presidente y afectará desde Irán e Israel hasta la posición global de EE UU

elpais.title: ¿Después de lo ‘woke’?
elpais.description: Todo lo que está triunfando ahora en las elecciones de EE UU se parece demasiado a lo que la socialdemocracia inventó aquí para luego abandonarlo

republika.title: Israele, a Eisekot l’incarico per il nuovo governo: “Se vogliono l’unità, Netanyahu mi sostenga”
republika.description: Il presidente israeliano ha conferito ufficialmente il mandato al leader del partito Yashar nel corso di una cerimonia presso la Residenza presidenziale a Gerusalemme. E apre anche al Partito Sionista

republika.title: White, dal ring alla Casa Bianca: chi è l’amico di Trump che potrebbe diventare il suo nuovo portavoce
republika.description: Per l’imprenditore che ha trasformato l’Ufc in un impero globale “siamo tutti lottatori”. L’amicizia con Donald iniziata quasi trent’anni fa, fu lui il primo a offrirgli ospitalità per gli incontri di MMA (arti marziali miste) nel suo hotel ad Atlantic City

republika.title: Donna di 71 anni uccisa in casa a Palosco: il figlio 47enne portato in caserma
republika.description: Carabinieri nella villetta di via Paolo VI della cittadina bergamasca. L’omicidio dovrebbe risalire a qualche giorno fa

republika.title: Dipiazza: “Se lanciano bombe carta a Trieste, io gli sparo in testa”. Le opposizioni: “Si dimetta”
republika.description: È polemica per le parole del sindaco di Forza Italia sugli incidenti avvenuti in città. La dem Serracchiani: “È gravissimo che un'istituzione evochi l'esecuzione. Ritiri le sue dichiarazioni”

republika.title: Lazio avanti con Frattesi, il Napoli la riprende con un autogol: 1-1. Gattuso resta in testa da solo
republika.description: Un tempo per parte e pari giusto al Maradona. Biancocelesti alla sosta da primi della classe, Allegri resta nel limbo della mediocrità

republika.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: “La mia fuga dal Brasile? Un segreto che mi porterò nella tomba”
republika.description: Da Miami, il figlio di Jair sta diffondendo accuse infondate di brogli elettorali e sta cercando di influenzare a distanza la politica del suo Paese, nonostante il suo partito non stia contestando i risultati delle elezioni

republika.title: Massimiliano Fuksas: “Good architecture should be for everyone, not just the rich”
republika.description: The Italian architect behind Rome’s iconic Cloud convention centre discusses the housing crisis, social inequality, his projects around the world and his daughter Elisa’s documentary

republika.title: Jannik Sinner: "The body is the only opponent you can never beat"
republika.description: The Italian tennis star who once described himself as "programmed" has had to reprogramme himself and change the shape of his existence. "I’d erase what I felt the day I left home."

republika.title: “Aveva 25 anni meno di me ma le dissi: Catherine sarò il padre dei tuoi figli”
republika.description: In questo brano, tratto dalla sua autobiografia “Una vita pazzesca” il divo racconta il primo incontro con sua moglie Catherine Zeta-Jones: “Avevo letto che le piacevano gli uomini maturi”

republika.title: Il Maestro, Margherita e il tempo presente
republika.description: Sessant’anni fa usciva postumo il capolavoro di Bulgakov superando decenni di censura. Il capolavoro della letteratura russa diventa una parabola sulla resistenza e la libertà. Da rileggere ora più che mai

republika.title: Alleati, veti e incognite. Il generale alla prova del governo post-Bibi
republika.description: Per sbloccare lo stallo e allargare la coalizione, possibile l’istituzione di un servizio civile obbligatorio che eviti la leva agli studenti religiosi e si possa applicare anche agli arabi

republika.title: Piogge e inondazioni su Gaza: “Ci lasciano morire di freddo”
republika.description: Una violenta perturbazione ha colpito 700mila persone, allagando i campi profughi e circa 70mila tende degli sfollati

republika.title: Miller, il bullo del presidente dall’attivismo alla Casa Bianca: “La moglie dietro la nomina”
republika.description: Kate, nota podcaster conservatrice ha mobilitato i vertici Maga affinché appoggiassero l’incarico a chief of staff

republika.title: Wescott: “Altro che placarsi, Donald non vuole mollare e si affida a uno staff di estremisti”
republika.description: L’ex capo economista di Bill Clinton analizza le ultime mosse del tycoon: “La scelta più incredibile è il nuovo capo di gabinetto”

republika.title: Crescita e mercati appesi all’IA, la scommessa che scuote il mondo
republika.description: Gli investimenti nei centri dati superano ogni boom infrastrutturale della storia e il crescente debito di Big Tech coinvolge nell’azzardo il settore finanziario. L’Fmi: un crollo trascinerebbe giù il Pil globale di un punto

republika.title: “Io, nipote di Mutolo ho scoperto la mafia dopo anni di silenzi”
republika.description: Vincenzo De Caro ha ricostruito in un film la storia della sua famiglia: “In casa c’erano sempre racconti in codice, ho voluto conoscere la verità”

republika.title: Anac, le opposizioni attaccano: “Altra figuraccia del governo”, Salvini: “Domani nuovo nome”
republika.description: Il vicepremier rivendica il diritto a indicare il nome nella spartizione decisa con gli alleati e difende la prima scelta: “Aveva i requisiti”

republika.title: Caso Altieri, la rissa sul successore delle correnti leghiste, Meloni: niente errori
republika.description: Da Veca a Grasso e Urraro, la rosa dei nomi per l’autorità tra veti incrociat. Pronta una “ricompensa” per Altieri dopo la rinuncia

nyt.title: For Trump and America, a Clear Election Verdict but a Murky Future
nyt.description: As Americans absorb a stunning new political reality, they face a gap between the time they effectively decided to be done with the president and the time he is actually done.

nyt.title: For Stephen Miller, Election Defeat Is No Reason to Back Down on Immigration Crackdown
nyt.description: The president’s new chief of staff has already demonstrated his intention to forge ahead with an agenda that many voters rejected.

nyt.title: Hakeem Jeffries, in Line to Become House Speaker, Promises Bold Agenda
nyt.description: The man in line to be the first Black speaker is a reserved moderate seen by activists on the left as too timid to take on President Trump. He says he’s “strongly positioned” to get things done.

nyt.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms on What Democrats Have to Do to Not Squander the Win
nyt.description: The governor-elect of Georgia is elated about her party’s victories in the South, but knows realignment is far from secure.

nyt.title: How Mississippi Reached the Verge of Electing a Black Senator
nyt.description: The echoes of history surround Scott Colom’s final push toward victory, but assembling the coalition that propelled him took hard work after many Democratic misses.

nyt.title: Top Astrophysicist Leaves U.S. After Trump Policies Affect Her Work
nyt.description: Kelly Holley-Bockelmann was one of the top astrophysicists in the country until President Trump’s policies affected every part of her work.

nyt.title: How Trump Is Dismantling America’s Scientific Research Machine
nyt.description: The system that has driven life-altering discoveries and helped make the United States a superpower is now under intense strain.

nyt.title: Who Is Gadi Eisenkot, Israel’s Opposition Leader?
nyt.description: Mr. Eisenkot, a career general and the leading rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, will now have up to six weeks to form a coalition.

nyt.title: After ‘Babydoll’, Dominic Fike Embraces the Mess
nyt.description: In the wake of a viral hit, new sobriety and fatherhood, the rocker scrapped the album he had been working on to make a less-polished LP.

nyt.title: Republicans Don’t Understand Men, Either
nyt.description: For the most part, young men want to be good men.

nyt.title: The Price of Child Stardom
nyt.description: We look at the dark side of K-pop.

nyt.title: Justice Dept. Mulled Naming The Times as Conspirator in Comey Leak Case
nyt.description: It remains unclear how the Justice Department might proceed. The move would be a major escalation of the Trump administration’s recent attacks against the news media.

npr.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
npr.description: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

npr.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
npr.description: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.

npr.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
npr.description: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

npr.title: A correspondent finds Cuba's people struggling
npr.description: Reporting from Cuba comes with distinct challenges especially amid widespread power outages and fuel shortages.

npr.title: Israel's president taps opposition candidate, not Netanyahu, to form a government
npr.description: Gadi Eisenkot ran as the main rival to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but neither won enough support to command a majority. Israel's main parties have recommended Eisenkot form a new government.

npr.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
npr.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

npr.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
npr.description: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.

npr.title: Pope Leo begins a 12-day, 3-country South America tour after his cancer surgery
npr.description: Pope Leo begins his first South American tour since lung cancer surgery. The 12-day journey takes him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades.

npr.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
npr.description: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization is warning its members to lock down systems following cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank.

npr.title: European flights and broadcasters are targeted with another wave of bomb threats
npr.description: Officials across Europe reported a slew of bomb threats against multiple flights, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. Three broadcasters also received threats.

lanacion.title: A qué hora llega el papa León XIV a la Argentina hoy, domingo 8 de noviembre
lanacion.description: El Sumo Pontífice arribará al país durante la tarde; cuál es el cronograma de su visita y las misas que dará

lanacion.title: Franco Colapinto, en el Gran Premio de Brasil de Fórmula 1: el minuto a minuto
lanacion.description: La carrera se desarrolla en el circuito brasileño de Interlagos; televisan Disney+ y Fox Sports

lanacion.title: Mamdani confirma nueva extensión de carril exclusivo para buses en Nueva York: “Estamos agilizando”
lanacion.description: Mamdani confirmó una nueva extensión de carriles exclusivos para buses en Nueva York y aseguró que ayudará a agilizar los traslados. Cómo será el proyecto, cuándo se implementará y qué zonas de la ciudad abarcará

lanacion.title: Papa León XIV en la Argentina, EN VIVO: a qué hora llega, la agenda del domingo y las últimas noticias hoy
lanacion.description: El Sumo Pontífice aterrizará 16.30 en el país; el minuto a minuto con todas sus actividades

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation

The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

phys-org.title: Game theory helps SETI search for alien civilizations
phys-org.description: The search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) is mostly concerned with where to look for technosignatures from another civilization. Between 2012 and 2015, SETI's Project Phoenix targeted about 1,000 sun-like stars for signs of intelligent life. But where to look might not be as important as when to look, according to scientists at SETI.

phys-org.title: 'Stupendously large' primordial black holes ruled out as a dark matter source
phys-org.description: Primordial black holes are hypothetical objects that could have formed directly from dense clumps of matter in the very early universe. If they exist, their dramatic origins would set them apart from the black holes we see today, which form when massive stars collapse. Some theories suggest that "stupendously large" primordial black holes could account for a significant share of the universe's elusive dark matter.

phys-org.title: Chimp sanctuary delivers an ape's food by drone amid Florida floods

phys-org.title: Why the tropics lose the most birds when cities expand
phys-org.description: Tropical ecosystems are famous for their teeming, exuberant diversity. In fact, the dramatic increase in biodiversity from the poles to the tropics—known as the latitudinal diversity gradient—is pervasive across branches of the tree of life, and fossil evidence suggests it has existed for millennia.

phys-org.title: Personalized savings reminders can help boost retirement savings
phys-org.description: Private retirement savings are an increasingly important topic in public debate. One popular idea is to phrase savings reminders in one of two ways: either you emphasize what someone stands to lose if they don't save, or you emphasize what they stand to gain if they do. To date, research into which of the two reminder messages is more effective in terms of influencing people's efforts to save has produced conflicting results.

phys-org.title: Student finds proof of rare wild cat in northern New Mexico

It was his first field season collecting photos for a two-year study to understand how forest structure influences biodiversity in the Southern Rocky Mountains.

phys-org.title: The hidden ways insects support animal life—from habitat to health—go way beyond being food
phys-org.description: There are at least 14 million insect species on Earth, and they play highly diverse roles in sustaining the natural world. Insects provide many well-known benefits—what scientists often call "ecosystem services." For example, you can thank a bee or a hoverfly for pollinating wildflowers and agricultural crops, or credit dung beetles for decomposing manure and other waste materials.

phys-org.title: Different text genres help doctoral students adapt their writing to reach new readers
phys-org.description: An academic abstract, a blog post and a public outreach article all place different demands on the writer. Readers' prior knowledge varies, as does the purpose of the text and what needs explaining. Mastering one kind of text therefore does not automatically mean being able to write another.

phys-org.title: Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory
phys-org.description: In a new Nature Physics study, researchers demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory using a hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer.

phys-org.title: Earth's gravity may have kept the early moon's volcanic heart beating
phys-org.description: We typically think of the moon as a static, floating object that has remained the same for basically its entire lifetime, with an occasional asteroid impact serving as an exception. phys-org.title: Scientists discover new jellyfish species in waters off Alicante in Spain

phys-org.title: Heavy rain can more than double glacier speeds in Alaska
phys-org.description: Glaciers are often thought of as unyielding blocks of ice that slowly carve out the landscape as they move downhill by gravity. But sometimes their slow crawl becomes a surge that sees them move orders of magnitude faster than their usual speed.

phys-org.title: The introduction of a medieval public health system exposed the population to roundworm
phys-org.description: Medieval health and sanitation efforts involved deliberate interventions; however, some of these measures had the opposite effect, leading to an increased spread of disease in Trondheim.

phys-org.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
phys-org.description: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.

phys-org.title: Why treating soil acidity crop by crop is no longer enough for prairie farmers
phys-org.description: To protect their future harvests, Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation rather than crop by crop, long-term research from the University of Alberta suggests.

phys-org.title: Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here's how to stay safer

phys-org.title: Polar vortex faltering weeks earlier than ever recorded
phys-org.description: Meteorologists said Friday they were observing an unprecedented early disruption of the polar vortex, raising the risk of cold snaps across the Northern Hemisphere, though there remains significant uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Defense And Space Tech Lead For Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: This week brought another plethora of large funding rounds for startups and growth-stage companies. Shield AI, a defense tech player focused on autonomy and virtual simulations, secured the largest financing, bringing in $2 billion. Next on the list was drone delivery provider Zipline International, which pulled in a fresh $1.5 billion.

crunchbase.title: How To Challenge A Monopoly In The AI Age
crunchbase.description: AI chip startups can challenge the sector's Goliath's by building substantially better hardware for emerging inference demands, much as Juniper challenged Cisco with a new architecture suited to the internet’s rapid growth. To win customers, writes guest author R K Anand, co-founder and chief product officer of Tensordyne, challengers must prove their advantages, make switching easy and use small, agile teams to anticipate needs that incumbents have yet to address.

crunchbase.title: General Catalyst Tops Lead Investors For October In Busy Month For US Startup Dealmaking
crunchbase.description: October was a busy month for U.S. startup funding, led by well-known venture investors with a healthy appetite for big deals. We take a look at active investor rankings across three categories: lead deal count, largest lead investments and total venture rounds.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Nurx And Journey Clinical Co-Founders Raise $6M For Mental Health Startup Siggy
crunchbase.description: Siggy has raised $6 million in pre-seed funding to build a mental health service that uses AI to collect patients’ histories and track progress between appointments with licensed clinicians, the startup told Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: Dropbox Plans $350M AI Infrastructure Deal With Tigris Buy, Its Biggest Acquisition Yet
crunchbase.description: Dropbox has announced plans to acquire Tigris Data for $350 million in a transaction the company told Crunchbase News would mark its largest acquisition since its founding in 2007.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Construction Robotics Funding Soars To $1.6B, Tripling Previous Peak
crunchbase.description: Companies spanning construction and robotics have raised about $1.6 billion so far this year  — more than 4x the $389 million recorded in all of 2025 — according to Crunchbase data. The surge was driven by three companies that raised the majority of the funding.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Less Than 2% Of 2026 Venture Funding Went To Post-Election Red States
crunchbase.description: So far this year, less than 2% of all startup investment has gone to companies in post-election red states, a share that is much smaller than in years past due to five states shifting to purple in the most recent election.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: Most Venture Capital Is Going To Companies That Are Founded Or Led By Billionaires
crunchbase.description: More than half of all seed- through growth-stage venture capital raised in the U.S. so far in 2026 went to seven companies founded or led by men who are already billionaires. Together, these companies raised more than $260 billion in equity funding in the first 10 months of the year.

crunchbase.title: China’s Largest Startup Deal Ever Lifts Global Venture Funding To $59B In October
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding in October totaled $59 billion, a 45% jump from a year earlier, per Crunchbase data, in large part due to a record-setting $15.9 billion funding round for China’s DeepSeek.
